newsitem.title: CANADA: IPSCO earnings boost Canadian steel stocks.
newsitem.headline: IPSCO earnings boost Canadian steel stocks.

text.p: Canadian steel stocks roared to new heights in early trading on Tuesday after IPSCO Inc surprised the market with higher than expected earnings, boosting bullish sentiment about the sector.
Shares in IPSCO jumped 2.85 to 53.25 in light mid-morning trade after the Regina-based steelmaker said its second-quarter earnings rose to C$1.11 a share from year earlier C$0.62.
Analysts said the strong earnings launch from IPSCO boded well for the rest of the sector, which hits its full earnings reporting stride next week.

"(IPSCO's results were) above my expectations. I was looking for C$1 (per share)...that's probably a sign of what's to come over the next couple of weeks in terms of earnings. I think this quarter is going to be very strong for the industry," said Greg Misztela, head of research at Griffiths McBurney Partners in Toronto.
IPSCO said results were boosted by firming prices and a shorter than usual spring breakup period, which translated into unexpectedly high oil patch tubular shipments in Canada.
Analysts have said the sector would lead profit growth in Canada this year, with per share growth pegged at 35 percent.
Co-Steel Inc is set to report second-quarter results July 21, followed by Stelco Inc and Dofasco Inc DOF.TO on July 23, Prudential Steel Ltd on July 27 and Algoma Steel Inc on July 29.

Stock in the steelmakers climbed in morning trade on Tuesday on the coattails of IPSCO, boosting the Toronto Stock Exchange's industrial sub-index 12.8 points, against the exchange's overall downtick.
"They're absolutely on wheels here because IPSCO's numbers were so strong," said Dunnery Best, director of private client investing at Toronto brokerage Midland Walwyn.
"A lot of people are going to say if IPSCO's numbers were strong like that, then that's going to translate into strength for the rest of the group," Best added.
Stelco led Toronto actives, gaining 0.50 to 12.35 as more than 2.1 million shares changed hands, while Prudential climbed 0.70 to 390 in block-dominated trade of 203,272 shares.
Co-Steel rose 0.55 to 24.60 on 239,000 shares and Dofasco rose 0.30 to 31.30 in lighter trade.
IPSCO has climbed more than 10 points in the past week, when it was trading near its 52-week high at 41.80, and the rest of the sector has charted similar climbs in recent days.
Misztela said stocks would likely remain strong through the third quarter.
"What's carrying the stocks is basically the momentum, and I think you're going to see very, very stong results this quarter and next quarter as well," he said.
